title: fix(runtime)!: an action not bound to an object accepts no record
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none (checked: skills/** — `objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md` and its evals teach `recordId` and `params._selectedIds` only for actions declared on an object; no published skill teaches a call that carries a record to an action not bound to an object)

## 维护者速读

- 调用方（界面、接口、AI 工具、宿主程序）调用一个不属于任何对象的动作时，若同时带上了某条记录或一批选中记录，现在会被直接拒绝并指明是哪一项；不带记录的调用照常运行。
- 安全加固：让「不属于任何对象的动作」不再接受记录，替维护者收口一处高危项。
- 若有调用方原本给这类动作带记录，会收到明确的 400 提示而不是被执行；该改动可整体撤回，撤回后恢复原行为。
- 无。

## What changes

An action not bound to an object accepts no record. A call to an action declared on no object that carries a `recordId` (in the body or the path) or a `params._selectedIds` is refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, the key named in `error.details.fields[0].field`, before any record is read and before the action runs. The rule is judged on the action's own declaration, so it holds whatever object the call is routed under, with or without a package namespace, and with no object at all; for every caller and every action type.

It is one check in the one admitted sequence every door shares, so it holds at REST `POST /api/v1/actions/...`, the MCP `run_action` tool and a host's `dispatchAction` alike. `packages/mcp` needs no change: its `run_action` reaches the same sequence.

Unchanged: an action declared on an object (in its `actions`, or standalone with its `objectName`) has its `recordId` loaded and its selection read in the caller's own scope first, as before; an object-less action called with neither key runs as before.

Files to read first, by risk:

1. `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` — `isObjectLessActionDeclaration` and `objectLessActionRecordKeyFailure`: what counts as "bound to an object" (the routed object's own `actions`, matched by reference or name, else the declaration's owner key).
2. `packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts` — the one new check in `admitResolvedAction`, after the body and record-key shape checks and before the selection read, the param contract and the subject load.
3. `packages/runtime/src/action-object-less-record-key.test.ts` — the new pins across the three doors.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/action-object-less-record-key.test.ts` prints `Tests 30 passed (30)`.

## Tests

New: `packages/runtime/src/action-object-less-record-key.test.ts` (30 cases). On each door (REST, `dispatchAction`, MCP `run_action`), an object-less action called with `_selectedIds`, and with `recordId`, is refused 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the key; a spy on the body shows it never ran, and no row of the routed object was read. Each is asserted with no object, under a real object's name, and (REST, `dispatchAction`) under a real object's name with the package namespace; MCP reaches an object-less action under an object's name by its namespace only. Preservation: the object-less action with neither key still runs on every route and door; an object-bound action with a readable selection still runs (every id read first); one unreadable id in its selection still refuses the whole call 404 `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`.

Updated, because they pinned the opposite of this rule (each now pins the rule, and keeps its own control):

- `action-door-record-load-denied.test.ts` — the three "object-less action invoked with a recordId still dispatches" cases now assert the 400 and that nothing ran; a new case keeps the record-less object-less call dispatching at both doors.
- `http-dispatcher.actions-global-key.test.ts` — the object-less record-id case asserts the 400, no load and no run.
- `action-declarative-update.test.ts` — the object-less declarative update keeps its own `objectName` refusal when called with no record, and is refused the 400 first when called with one.
- `domains/actions-addressed-route.test.ts` — the addressed record-id case asserts the 400 at REST and MCP, with nothing read and nothing run.
- `stored-metadata-reader-contexts.pin.test.ts` — the object-less cases under the metadata tables assert the 400; the host-handler control now uses a handler declared on the table, which is still handed the row the data door serves.

Reverse verification (one-off, no permanent file): with the new check removed from the admitted sequence (committed fix, mutation through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor 1 to 0, restored blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty), the new file goes 13 failed / 17 passed; restored, 30 passed.

## Acceptance notes

- **File surface widened by one file, on the dispatching seat's ruling:** `packages/runtime/src/domains/actions-addressed-route.test.ts`, one case only ("the same CALL on both doors, with a record id"), test-only. It pinned the earlier answer for an object-less action called with a record id; it now pins this rule at both doors (400 naming `recordId`, nothing read, nothing run).
- A caller that sends a record key to an action declared on no object now gets the 400 instead of a run. To act on records, declare the action on their object.
